rows.stem: Which one of the following organ is **NOT** a part of human female reproductive system ?
rows.solution:
The human female reproductive system consists of the ovaries, the fallopian tubes (oviducts), the uterus and the vagina. The vas deferens is part of the male reproductive system: it carries sperms from the testis towards the urethra.

This is option (C) Vas deferens.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: In bifocal lenses used for the correction of presbyopia :

options.label: A
options.text: the upper portion is of convex lens for the near vision and lower part is of concave lens for the distant vision.

options.label: B
options.text: the upper portion is of convex lens for the distant vision and lower part is of concave lens for the near vision.

options.label: C
options.text: the upper portion is of concave lens is for the near vision and lower part is of convex lens for the distant vision.

options.label: D
options.text: the upper portion is of concave lens for the distant vision and lower part is of convex lens for the near vision.

rows.solution:
A person with presbyopia often has both myopia and hypermetropia, so needs a lens of each kind. A myopic eye is corrected with a concave lens, used for seeing distant objects, and a hypermetropic eye with a convex lens, used for reading and other near work. In a bifocal lens the upper portion, which the eye looks through at distant objects, is the concave lens, and the lower portion, used for reading, is the convex lens.

This is option (D) the upper portion is of concave lens for the distant vision and lower part is of convex lens for the near vision.

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem:
(i) Write the significance of peripheral nervous system in human beings.

(ii) How is human brain protected from mechanical injuries and shocks ?
rows.solution:
(i) The peripheral nervous system is made of the cranial nerves arising from the brain and the spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord. It links the central nervous system with all the other parts of the body: it carries messages from the receptors to the brain and spinal cord, and from them to the muscles and glands. So it makes communication between the central nervous system and the rest of the body possible.

(ii) The brain sits inside a bony box, the skull (cranium). Inside the box it is contained in a fluid-filled balloon, and this fluid acts as a shock absorber, protecting the brain from mechanical injuries and shocks.

rows.stem: Name one directional growth movement each in response to chemicals and water in plants. Write an example for each of them.
rows.solution:
Chemotropism is directional growth in response to chemicals. Example: the growth of pollen tubes towards the ovules.

Hydrotropism is directional growth in response to water. Example: the growth of roots towards water.

rows.stem:
(i) Give reason why herbivorous animals have longer, small intestine than carnivorous animals ?

(ii) Although ‘Pepsin’ and ‘Trypsin’ are both protein digesting enzymes yet they differ from each other. Justify this statement by giving one difference between them.
rows.solution:
(i) Herbivores eat grass, which contains cellulose, and cellulose takes a long time to digest. A longer small intestine gives the food more time for the cellulose to be digested. Meat is easier to digest, so carnivores such as tigers have a shorter small intestine.

(ii) Any one difference:

| Pepsin | Trypsin |
|---|---|
| Secreted by the gastric glands in the wall of the stomach | Secreted by the pancreas (in the pancreatic juice) |
| Acts in an acidic medium in the stomach | Acts in an alkaline medium in the small intestine |

rows.stem:
Translate the following statement into a balanced chemical equation.

“When barium chloride reacts with aluminium sulphate, aluminium chloride and barium sulphate are formed.”

State the type of this reaction giving reason to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: prints \(\mathrm{2BaCl_2(aq) + Al_2(SO_4)_3(aq) \rightarrow 2AlCl_3(aq) + 3BaSO_4(s)}\), which is not balanced (2 barium and 4 chlorine atoms on the left, 3 and 6 on the right); the balanced equation needs 3 \(\mathrm{BaCl_2}\).]

\(\mathrm{3BaCl_2(aq) + Al_2(SO_4)_3(aq) \rightarrow 2AlCl_3(aq) + 3BaSO_4(s)}\)

Check: Ba 3 = 3; Cl 6 = 6; Al 2 = 2; S 3 = 3; O 12 = 12.

It is a double displacement reaction, because the two reactants exchange ions: barium combines with the sulphate and aluminium with the chloride. It is also a precipitation reaction, because the barium sulphate formed is insoluble and separates out as a white precipitate.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines due to a straight current carrying conductor indicating the direction of current in the conductor and the direction of the corresponding magnetic field lines.
rows.solution:
The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor are concentric circles, centred on the conductor, in a plane perpendicular to it. The direction of the field lines is given by the right-hand thumb rule.

Diagram: draw a straight vertical wire passing through a horizontal sheet of cardboard and connected in a circuit with a battery. Draw an arrow on the wire pointing upwards to show the direction of the current. On the cardboard, draw several concentric circles centred on the wire, closer together near the wire and farther apart away from it. Put arrows on the circles pointing anticlockwise as seen from above, which is the direction of the magnetic field for an upward current (if the current is reversed, the arrows point clockwise). Label "direction of current" on the wire and "direction of magnetic field lines" on a circle.

rows.stem:
(i) Which organisms have a three-chambered heart ? Why do they have three-chambered hearts ?

(ii) List two functions of lymph.
rows.solution:
(i) Amphibians such as frogs, and many reptiles such as lizards, have a three-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle).

These animals are cold-blooded: their body temperature depends on the temperature of the environment, so they do not use energy to keep the body warm and need less energy. They can therefore tolerate some mixing of the oxygenated and deoxygenated blood streams in the single ventricle, and a three-chambered heart is enough for them.

(ii) Any two functions of lymph:

1. It carries digested and absorbed fat from the intestine.

2. It drains excess fluid from the extracellular spaces back into the blood.

3. Its lymphocytes help to fight infection.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem:
A compound which is prepared from gypsum has the property of hardening when water is mixed in right quantity with it :

(i) Write common name and the chemical name of this compound.

(ii) Give chemical equation for its preparation.

(iii) List its two uses.
rows.solution:
(i) The compound is Plaster of Paris. Its chemical name is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O}\).

(ii) It is prepared by heating gypsum at 373 K, when gypsum loses part of its water of crystallisation:

\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O \xrightarrow{373\,K} CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O}\)

(When mixed with water, Plaster of Paris changes back to gypsum, which sets as a hard solid mass.)

(iii) Any two uses:

1. For supporting fractured bones in the right position (plaster casts by doctors).

2. For making toys.

3. For making materials for decoration.

4. For making surfaces smooth.

rows.stem:
(i) Define a decomposition reaction. Write chemical equation for the reaction that occurs when lead nitrate is heated strongly in a boiling tube.

(ii) In electrolytic decomposition of water two gases are liberated at the electrodes. Give the mass ratio of the gas liberated at the cathode and at the anode.
rows.solution:
(i) A decomposition reaction is one in which a single reactant breaks down to give two or more simpler products, usually by absorbing energy in the form of heat, light or electricity.

When lead nitrate is heated strongly, it decomposes into lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide (brown fumes) and oxygen:

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

Check: Pb 2 = 2; N 4 = 4; O 12 = 2 + 8 + 2.

(ii) Hydrogen is liberated at the cathode and oxygen at the anode:

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

Two molecules of hydrogen (mass \(2 \times 2 = 4\) u) are formed for every molecule of oxygen (mass 32 u). So the mass ratio of the gas at the cathode to the gas at the anode is \(4 : 32 = 1 : 8\). (By volume the ratio is \(2 : 1\).)

rows.stem:
(i) State whether the currents and potential difference in all the bulbs will be same or different when in a circuit three bulbs of :

(a) same wattage are connected in series.

(b) same wattage are connected in parallel.

(c) different wattage are connected in series.

(d) different wattage are connected in parallel.

(ii) Two identical resistors of \(24\,\Omega\) each are connected to a battery of 6 V. Calculate the ratio of the power consumed by the resulting combinations with (a) minimum resistance and (b) maximum resistance.
rows.solution:
(i) Take the bulbs to be rated for the same voltage, so a bulb of higher wattage has a lower resistance.

(a) Same wattage, in series: the same current flows through all the bulbs, and since their resistances are equal, the potential difference across each is also the same.

(b) Same wattage, in parallel: the potential difference across each bulb is the same, and since their resistances are equal, the current through each is also the same.

(c) Different wattage, in series: the current is the same, but the potential differences are different, since \(V = IR\) and the resistances differ.

(d) Different wattage, in parallel: the potential difference is the same, but the currents are different, since \(I = \dfrac{V}{R}\) and the resistances differ.

(ii) (a) The resistance is minimum when the two resistors are connected in parallel:

\(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{24} + \dfrac{1}{24} = \dfrac{2}{24}\), so \(R_p = 12\,\Omega\).

\(P_1 = \dfrac{V^2}{R_p} = \dfrac{6 \times 6}{12} = 3\) W.

(b) The resistance is maximum when they are connected in series:

\(R_s = 24 + 24 = 48\,\Omega\).

\(P_2 = \dfrac{V^2}{R_s} = \dfrac{6 \times 6}{48} = \dfrac{3}{4}\) W.

The ratio of the power consumed is

\(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2} = \dfrac{3}{3/4} = \dfrac{4}{1}\), so \(P_1 : P_2 = 4 : 1\).

rows.stem:
Draw a schematic diagram of a circuit consisting of a battery of six 2V cells, a \(6\,\Omega\) resistor, a \(12\,\Omega\) resistor and a \(18\,\Omega\) resistor and a plug key all connected in series. Calculate the following (when key is closed) :

(i) Electric current flowing in the circuit.

(ii) Potential difference across \(18\,\Omega\) resistor.

(iii) Electric power consumed in \(18\,\Omega\) resistor.
rows.solution:
Circuit diagram: draw a battery of six 2 V cells joined in series (six pairs of long and short lines, with + and - marked at the ends), and connect it in a single loop with the \(6\,\Omega\), \(12\,\Omega\) and \(18\,\Omega\) resistors (each drawn as a zig-zag line and labelled) and a plug key, one after the other, all in series.

The voltage of the battery is \(V = 6 \times 2 = 12\) V, and the total resistance is

\(R = 6 + 12 + 18 = 36\,\Omega\).

(i) Current in the circuit: \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{12}{36} = \dfrac{1}{3}\) A (about 0.33 A).

(ii) Potential difference across the \(18\,\Omega\) resistor: \(V = IR = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 18 = 6\) V.

(iii) Power consumed in the \(18\,\Omega\) resistor: \(P = VI = 6 \times \dfrac{1}{3} = 2\) W. (Equally, \(P = I^2R = \dfrac{1}{9} \times 18 = 2\) W.)
